# Postgres to Apache Doris

[Apache Doris](https://doris.apache.org/) is a columnar analytical database: it stores each column
separately, which makes scans and aggregates over many rows fast. It speaks the MySQL protocol.
Since version 4.1 it can follow Postgres by itself. One statement creates the target tables, copies
the existing rows and then streams changes from a replication slot, with no Kafka or Debezium to
deploy in between:

```sql
CREATE JOB pg_mirror_job
PROPERTIES ("max_interval" = "1")
ON STREAMING
FROM POSTGRES (
    "jdbc_url" = "jdbc:postgresql://db:5432/app",
    "driver_url" = "https://repo1.maven.org/maven2/org/postgresql/postgresql/42.7.4/postgresql-42.7.4.jar",
    "driver_class" = "org.postgresql.Driver",
    "user" = "app", "password" = "...",
    "database" = "app", "schema" = "doris_src",
    "include_tables" = "docs",
    "offset" = "initial"
)
TO DATABASE pg_mirror ("table.create.properties.replication_num" = "1");
```

## What the lab found

The lab runs one Doris frontend and one backend next to pg16, and points a job at the project's
tables. On Doris 4.1.4:

| | |
|---|---|
| source side | the job creates its own publication and slot, one per job; `DROP JOB` removes both |
| latency | seconds, not milliseconds: about 11 with the default `max_interval` of 10, about 5 with 1 |
| types | `jsonb` lands as `text`, `uuid` as `text`, `timestamptz` as `datetime(6)` in the Doris time zone |
| `vector` | auto table creation refuses it; in a pre-created table it arrives as NULL, silently |
| generated columns | copied by the snapshot, then dropped once streaming starts |
| DDL | added and dropped columns propagate, which Postgres to Postgres does not do |

The trade against the [previous chapter](logical-replication.qmd) is latency for convenience.
Changes take seconds to arrive instead of milliseconds, but schema changes come across on their
own.

## The vector problem

Doris's CDC client is Debezium's Postgres connector, and Debezium has no converter for pgvector's
`vector` type. The column does not fail; it arrives as NULL. The notebook verifies a workaround: a
trigger on the source keeps a `real[]` copy of each embedding. That copy arrives as `ARRAY<FLOAT>`,
and Doris's own `cosine_distance` then returns the same top five as pgvector.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Sized for a server

The images are large (4 GB for the frontend, 9 GB for the backend), and their defaults assume a
dedicated machine: an 8 GB heap, and a backend sized to 90% of memory. On Docker Desktop that ends
in `MEM_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`. The lab's compose file caps both (`DORIS_FE_HEAP`, `DORIS_BE_MEM`) so they
fit beside the other containers.
:::

Notebook: [Doris CDC](../notebooks/doris_cdc.ipynb), started with `just db doris`.
